input: Create /etc/env.conf with variable assignments: APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, APP_SECRET=s3cret123. Source this file. Export all three variables. Then write a script /scripts/check_env.sh that reads these environment variables and prints them as 'APP_ENV=<value>' (one per line). Run the script with bash and verify the environment variables propagated correctly. Also run 'env | grep APP_' to list all APP_ prefixed env vars.

transcript.final_response:
Created `/etc/env.conf`, sourced it, and exported all three variables. Created `/scripts/check_env.sh` and ran it with `bash`, confirming the variables propagated:

```text
APP_ENV=production
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_SECRET=s3cret123
```

`env | grep APP_` returned:

```text
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_ENV=production
APP_SECRET=s3cret123
```
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /etc /scripts
cat > /etc/env.conf <<'EOF'
APP_ENV=production
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_SECRET=s3cret123
EOF
source /etc/env.conf
export APP_ENV APP_DEBUG APP_SECRET
cat > /scripts/check_env.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf 'APP_ENV=%s\n' "$APP_ENV"
printf 'APP_DEBUG=%s\n' "$APP_DEBUG"
printf 'APP_SECRET=%s\n' "$APP_SECRET"
EOF
bash /scripts/check_env.sh
if [[ "$APP_ENV" == production && "$APP_DEBUG" == false && "$APP_SECRET" == s3cret123 ]]; then
  printf 'Parent environment values verified.\n'
fi
printf '\nExported APP_ variables:\n'
env | grep APP_
